title: Automated on-chip imaging and sorting of C. elegans
protocol: Spin-coat SU8-2025 on a silicon wafer at 3000 rpm for the worm loading layer.
Soft bake the wafer at 95°C for 5 min and UV-expose the photoresist with a mask for the worm loading layer.
Hard bake at 95°C for 7 min and develop the wafer with SU8 developer.
Spin-coat AZ50XT on the wafer at 2200 rpm.
Use a mask of AZ features for UV exposure.
After development with AZ 400T developer, heat the wafer at 125°C for 5 min to reflow the AZ photoresist.
Spin-coat SU8-2050 on a silicon wafer at 3000 rpm for the control layer.
Soft bake the wafer at 95°C for 5 min and UV-expose with a mask for the control layer.
Hard bake at 95°C for 7 min and develop the wafer with SU8 developer.
Spin-coat SU8-2025 on a silicon wafer at 3000 rpm for the filtering device.
Soft bake the wafer at 95°C for 5 min and UV-expose with a mask for the filtering device.
Hard bake at 95°C for 7 min and develop the wafer.
Treat two molds and a blank wafer with tridecafluoro-1,1,2,2-tetrahydrooctyl-1-trichlorosilane vapor in a vacuum desiccator at room temperature for at least 4 hours.
Prepare Mixture #1 of PDMS (A and B in 5:1 ratio) and Mixture #2 of PDMS (A and B and Toluene in 20:1:10.5 ratio) in a chemical hood.
Pour Mixture #1 onto the control-layer master to obtain a 5 mm-thick layer in a 15-mm Petri dish.
Bake the Petri dish for 20 minutes at 70 °C to make PDMS layer 1.
Spin-coat Mixture #2 onto the blank wafer to give a ~20 μm-thick layer.
Bake the coated wafer for 10 minutes at 70 °C to cure it.
Peel off the PDMS layer 1 from the master and place it on the PDMS membrane.
Fully cure the combined PDMS layer for 2 hours at 70 °C for bonding.
Spin-coat Mixture #1 onto the worm-loading layer master to give a 60 μm-thick layer.
Bake this layer for 2 hours at 70 °C to give PDMS layer 2.
Peel off the PDMS layer 2 from the master and flip it over.
Align the combined PDMS layer and bond it onto the flipped PDMS layer 2 using oxygen plasma treatment.
Punch holes in the bonded PDMS layers.
Bond the punched PDMS layers onto a cover glass.
Pour the mixture onto the filtering device master to obtain a 5 mm-thick layer in a 15-mm Petri dish.
Bake the dish for 2 hours at 70°C.
Peel off the PDMS layer and punch holes.
Bond the PDMS layer onto the cover glass using plasma treatment.
Bleach adults using bleaching solution for ~5 min \[ref 3].
Transfer hatched first larval stage animals on NGM plates seeded with E. coli OP50 after letting embryos hatch in M9 buffer for ~12 hr.
Culture the animals to the stage of interest.
Wash out animals from the NGM plate using M9 solution containing 0.5 % wt/vol BSA and spin down and wash three times with the M9 solution to remove E. coli.
Flow the worm suspension through the filtering device to remove debris.
Connect tubings and pins to the device properly and mount it on the stage of the microscope.
Prime the device with the buffer solution (M9).
Set up cooling system.
Pump coolant through tubing adjacent to the Peltier device.
Make sure there is no leakage.
Check that the valves work properly.
Measure the coolant temperature at the cooling inlet using a thermocouple.
Run the Matlab code.
Inject worm suspension into the device using pressure driven flow.
Flush the lines with buffer after imaging/sorting to collect animals.
Spin down the suspensions in the collection tubes.
Transfer animals onto NGM plates seeded with _E. coli_ OP50.
